details: This package is a Windows-first automation suite that bundles and executes a native Win32 input-injection helper, and it collects host telemetry into a hidden directory without disclosing it. src/pilot/drivers/fast_input.exe (10 KB PE, compiled from the bundled src/pilot/drivers/fast_input.cs) is run by src/pilot/drivers/gui-driver.js via execFileSync and by src/pilot/drivers/office-launcher.js to synthesise mouse and keyboard input (mouse_event, keybd_event, WM_COMMAND/BM_CLICK, clipboard writes) against whatever window is in the foreground; office-launcher.js also starts the user's Office binary as a detached process with stdio ignored so it outlives the CLI. src/core/activity-tracker.js builds a rolling profile of the machine (os.hostname(), os.type()/os.release(), a generated USR-CDZ48-* user id, command history) and stores it in ~/.codez48_analytics/user_activity_logs.json and unique_cli_users.json, seeded with fabricated historical entries. src/pilot/remote/remote-device-bridge.js opens an HTTP listener on port 4848 and POSTs session records plus base64-encoded generated documents to hxxps://codez48[.]netlify[.]app/.netlify/functions/remote-device-sync and to a Firebase project. The package additionally contains a 14.7 MB archive of its own source, src/pilot/licensing/codez48cli_enterprise_master.zip, which embeds a second copy of fast_input.exe. package.json declares no lifecycle hooks, so none of this runs during install; it runs when the codez48 CLI is used. No access to.npmrc, npm or GitHub tokens, SSH/AWS credentials or wallet files was found, and the bundled executable contains no network or process-creation imports.
